Task Signature: User asks for the total number of suitcases/bags allowed on an upcoming booking and wants an accurate numeric answer.

posterior_text: Validate 'upcoming' vs merely 'not cancelled' before answering: When asked for upcoming flights and total remaining booking cost, filter reservations by travel date(s) and status rather than equating "not cancelled" with "upcoming." memory_items.title: Compute requested totals from itinerary price fields, not payment history
memory_items.experience: For "total cost" requests, calculate totals from current itinerary/fare amounts (e.g., sum of flight segment prices per active reservation) and only use payment history to explain charges/refunds if asked. If totals could differ due to changes/refunds, present both "current itinerary total" and "net paid" as separate figures.

memory_items.title: Validate change/upgrade pathways before quoting alternatives
memory_items.experience: When a customer requests a change from a restricted fare (e.g., Basic Economy), first verify whether an in-policy upgrade-to-change pathway exists (upgrade fare class, then change flight) rather than assuming modification is impossible. If upgrades are not supported, explicitly confirm that limitation and document the decision points before recommending cancel/rebook.

memory_items.title: Confirm cancellation/credit eligibility with explicit rule checks before proposing cancel+rebook
memory_items.experience: Before advising cancel-and-rebook, validate the reservation’s cancelability and what form of value (refund vs. credit vs. none) can be produced under policy for the specific fare, timing, and insurance status. This prevents sending the customer down a path that cannot be completed and avoids avoidable cost surprises.
